transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Lawmakers returned to Capitol Hill this week for a lame-dex session following last week's midterms.
Democrats are preparing to take control of the House and Senate in January.
NPR's Eric McDaniel explains how the party could begin laying the groundwork for its agenda.
They have the authority to force documents to be turned over to make people come and testify under oath
to hold people accountable in the courts if they refuse.
And these have been used to great effect through U.S. history, right?
The Watergate-era investigations exposed big cover-up schemes by the Nixon administration.
And with government corruption at the top of the list of voter concerns,
it makes sense that this would be a tool Democrats are prioritizing.
That's NPR's Eric McDaniel reporting.
In the meantime, the current Congress has several pieces of unfinished business.
Government funding expires on December 11th,
and spending negotiations are expected to resume this week to avoid a government shutdown.
Russia is stepping up attacks on Ukraine's power grid ahead of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi this week.
The latest round of airstrikes has left hundreds of thousands of people without electricity,
as NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports.
The attacks are part of the Kremlin's strategy to freeze Ukrainians and leave them in the dark.
This winter, a regional military spokesperson said Ukraine's power company, D-Tech,
is working to restore electricity, but efforts are being hampered by constant Russian shelling.
Alexander Hanza said hospitals had been forced to switch to diesel generators,
and electric-powered public transport had ground to a halt in the large eastern city of Nipro.
President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of seeking to apply maximum pressure
ahead of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi in the coming days by, quote,
"plunging the entire country into a blackout."
Russia began stepping up attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure in late September.
It has targeted the sector every winter since launching its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Kyiv.
Crowds of Christian faithful gathered over the weekend in Uruguay to welcome Pope Leo.
NPR's Kerry Kahn reports the pontiff will continue his South American tour with the trip today to Argentina.
Pope Leo hasn't shied away from taking on Uruguay's tightly enforced division between church and state.
In a poor community outside the capital Montevedeo, Leo urged more cooperation
between the church, civil society, and the government to help the poor.
The city of Nipro has to be part of the 60th century,
and we have to be part of the 60th century.
We must awaken from our inertia and advocate together for the common good.
Speaking to his largest gathering in Montevedeo's historic football stadium,
Leo said the government does have a role, but nothing compares to God's love.
Kerry Kahn, NPR News, Montevedeo.
This is NPR News in Washington.
One person was killed and more than a dozen others were injured when a car hit a group of cyclists in North Carolina on Saturday.
Leroy Smith is the fire chief of Wake County.
Early hours of the day or whenever, just be aware of people that are out riding bikes.
They have rights to be on the road too, so kind of yield to them and be cautious when you're riding around bicycles.
Authorities say the 76-year-old driver was impaired and has been taken into custody.
Celebrations are taking place around the world, marking Diwali, one of India's biggest holidays,
and PR Shandali Stuster reports on festivities taking place here in the United States.
Known as the Festival of Lights, Diwali began in India more than 2,000 years ago.
While it is a major Hindu festival, it's also celebrated by other religions such as Jains and Sikhs.
With more than 5 million people of Indian origin living in the U.S.,
more and more cities are hosting public events to celebrate what's known as the victory of light over darkness.
In downtown Seattle, community groups offered free vegetarian meals, classical Indian dancing, and cow cuddling.
There were celebrations on the East Coast, including in Edison, New Jersey, where there was also food, dancing, and 100,000 lights on display.
Shandali Stuster and PR News.
At least 22 people were injured when a strong earthquake hit central to Penn today.
The magnitude 5.7 quake shattered store windows and sent books tumbling from shelves.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.

Drink responsibly, B21.

topics.text: Democrats prepare to take House and Senate control in January; Eric McDaniel explains oversight powers
Government funding expires December 11th, with spending negotiations expected to resume this week
Russia steps up attacks on Ukraine's power grid ahead of U.S.-mediated Abu Dhabi talks
Pope Leo draws crowds in Uruguay, urges church, government, and civil society cooperation to aid the poor
One killed, more than a dozen injured when car hits cyclists in Wake County, North Carolina
Diwali celebrations held across U.S. cities, including Seattle and Edison, New Jersey
Magnitude 5.7 earthquake in central Peru injures at least 22 people and shatters store windows
